title: How Much Do Medical Interpreters Cost?
summary: Medical interpreter services cost more than sticker rates show. Learn what drives real pricing, hidden fees, and how to reduce spend in 2026.
body_markdown:
###


Over-the-phone interpretation runs roughly $1 to $3 per minute for common languages, video remote interpretation starts around $1.95 per minute, and AI interpretation platforms like Opalite Health price below traditional per-minute rates while covering 150+ languages and dialects instantly. The sticker rate rarely reflects true cost per completed encounter once you account for billed silence, hourly minimums, and rush premiums layered underneath.


###


Silent-time billing, one-to-two hour on-site minimums, portal-to-portal travel charges, and hold time for rare-language connections all inflate the invoice above the per-minute rate on the contract. A 20-minute visit billed against a two-hour minimum is paying for 100 minutes of interpretation that never happened.


###


Build a tiered routing policy that sends routine follow-ups and administrative calls to phone or AI interpretation, reserves on-site services for encounters where physical presence adds clear clinical value, and names explicit escalation criteria for patient preference. Carolinas Healthcare System reported $1.5 million in annual savings after shifting to remote interpreter technology, and consolidating vendors under volume-based pricing removes the overlapping minimums that quietly double the bill.


###


Medicaid does not require states to reimburse providers for language services, and interpretation is not a mandatory benefit under Section 1905 of the Social Security Act. Some states have elected to cover it, but coverage varies widely and many providers receive nothing back from the payer. Private insurers rarely include interpreter reimbursement in their contracts. The cost lands on the provider's budget regardless of payer mix. Federal civil rights law still requires covered organizations to make qualified language services available at no cost to the patient, so the financial obligation does not disappear. It just goes uncompensated.


###


Silent-time billing means your phone or video interpreter contract charges for every connected minute, including pauses while the provider documents, physical exams, and any portion of the visit where no interpretation is happening. For a 30-minute encounter with 10 minutes of active interpretation, you may be billed for all 30. Organizations can address this in two ways: renegotiate contract language to exclude non-interpretation minutes, or move to an AI interpretation platform structured around active use rather than total connected time. Either path requires a contract review, but the savings on even a mid-volume site can exceed several thousand dollars per month.
